public_rationale: Anthropic's filing provides a credible mechanism: some compute commitments cannot be cancelled simply because usage falls. That can make a slowdown costly. It does not establish that the combined commitments make a defined slowdown deeply impractical. Anthropic also reported a limited training pause, showing that some restraint was possible. The scale, duration and net financial burden needed to settle the causal claim remain unspecified or unmeasured.
limitations: A contract's size and cancellation terms do not alone establish financial impracticality.
The filing contains later amendments elsewhere; those were not treated as publication-date obligations.
The scoped pause does not test a sustained reduction in total compute demand.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that existing compute obligations make a substantial slowdown economically difficult because sizeable payments would remain unavoidable.
Deeply impractical does not mean impossible. A brief pause is not enough to test a sustained slowdown.
The causal assessment concerns commitments in force on September 14, 2026. Later disclosures may document earlier agreements, but subsequent amendments must be excluded.
The surrounding discussion relies on reported estimates of lab commitments. It does not specify GAAP or another accounting basis.
As it stands anchors the assessment to publication; it is not a future antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Contracts in force at publication, together with cash-flow evidence, show that a substantial slowdown would leave unavoidable payments large enough to make the slowdown economically difficult.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contractual flexibility, replacement workloads or demonstrable savings establish that the commitments would not materially obstruct a substantial slowdown.
